withdrawal_reasons: The alpha condition is satisfiable only inside the excluded phi window, so no non-phi base can pass whatever the lepton or proton results; the zero-hit count carries no information about phi.

No p-value or sigma is reported; the earlier p_null bound and its sigma conversion are withdrawn.
cross_base_monte_carlo.verdict: WITHDRAWN-NON-INFORMATIVE — 0 non-phi bases hit all four bare targets, as forced by construction: the alpha condition admits only b in [1.61558, 1.62043], inside the excluded window [1.60803, 1.62803]. No significance is claimed.

withdrawal_reasons: The 21 ppm hit window equals the observed muon residual, so it was fixed after the data were seen.
Only phi is evaluated; the grid says nothing about phi against other constants.
The C2 step alpha^2 (about 5.3e-5) is comparable to the window width (about 4.2e-5), so the (C1, C2) grid is effectively a covering and the hit fraction measures grid volume, not specialness.
The earlier run used a stale tau target (3477.15); the target is PDG 2024.
lepton_exponent_pair.note: Diagnostic only. No sigma is computed; the earlier expanded-grid sigma is withdrawn.

joint_4param_monte_carlo.note: The cross-base bare-control test is non-informative by construction (see cross_base_monte_carlo.withdrawal_reasons).

headline_significance: None. Earlier global-significance figures for the numerical matches are withdrawn: the cross-base comparison could not, by construction, credit any base other than phi, and the trial counts behind the quoted sigma values were asserted rather than enumerated. The preregistered constant control test that compares phi against other constants under identical formula freedom has reported: v3 is NEGATIVE-FRAGILE (p0 = 0.196; 58 of 300 random bases do at least as well as phi on the 21 constants; non-confirmatory). The phi-formula matches are therefore Tier 4 as evidence that phi explains the value (constant control test v3 NEGATIVE-FRAGILE; App PSC §PSC.9.6).
